legend: Henrique wants to park his car in the parking lot of the University of Brasília (UnB).

The parking spots are numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$. Spot number i$$$i$$$ is characterized by two numbers: its distance di$$$d_i$$$ from the main entrance and the probability pi$$$p_i$$$ that it is free. Henrique visits the spots sequentially, starting from spot 1$$$1$$$. Upon arriving at spot i$$$i$$$, two situations may occur:

With probability pi$$$p_i$$$, spot i$$$i$$$ is free. In this case, Henrique has two options: park in spot i$$$i$$$ (Henrique is extremely fast, so we may consider that he takes 0$$$0$$$ seconds to park), or move on to the next spot, which is spot i+1$$$i+1$$$ if i≠n$$$i \neq n$$$ and spot 1$$$1$$$ if i=n$$$i = n$$$.
With probability 1−pi$$$1-p_i$$$, spot i$$$i$$$ is occupied. In this case, Henrique is forced to continue to the next spot.

Each time Henrique moves on to the next spot, he spends 1$$$1$$$ second. After visiting spot i$$$i$$$ once, it is possible that in subsequent visits its state will be different, since the UnB parking lot is very busy and a driver may have occupied or vacated the spot during the time Henrique took to return to it. This behaviour will be dictated by the probability pi$$$p_i$$$, which remains fixed throughout the entire problem.

Henrique wants to act so that the expected value of the sum of the total time spent choosing a spot and the distance of the spot where he finally parks is as small as possible. If Henrique acts optimally, what is this value?
input: The first line of the input contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤3⋅105)$$$(2 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5)$$$.
The second line of the input contains n$$$n$$$ integers d1,d2,…,dn$$$d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n$$$ (1≤di≤106)$$$(1 \leq d_i \leq 10^6)$$$.

Finally, the third line of the input contains n$$$n$$$ real numbers p1,p2,…,pn$$$p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n$$$ (0.001≤pi≤1)$$$(0.001 \leq p_i \leq 1)$$$. Each pi$$$p_i$$$ is given with at most 3 decimal places.
output: Print a single real number: the expected value of the sum of the total time spent choosing a spot and the distance of the spot where he parks under the best strategy. Your answer will be considered correct if the absolute or relative error does not exceed 10−6$$$10^{-6}$$$. That is, if your answer is a$$$a$$$ and the correct answer is b$$$b$$$, your answer will be accepted if and only if |a−b|max(1,|b|)≤10−6$$$\frac{|a-b|}{\operatorname{max}(1, |b|)} \le 10^{-6}$$$.
note: In the first test case, Henrique should park in spot number 4$$$4$$$. He takes a total of 3$$$3$$$ seconds to reach it, and it is at a distance of 4$$$4$$$ meters from the entrance, so the sum of the time spent and the distance is 3+4=7$$$3 + 4 = 7$$$. Since all spots are always free, he always achieves this value.
